# ADR-0089: Bound optional Claude start-refusal diagnosis

Status: Accepted under delegated delivery decision D203, 2026-11-21.

## Context

After a native spawn refusal with no child PID, the Claude runner knows that nothing
was submitted. Read-only filesystem observations can distinguish a missing absolute
executable or missing/file working directory from an unknown cause (#364). Waiting
for those optional observations must not postpone the known failure indefinitely.
Normal turns have no request timeout, and the inference watchdog and run deadline
are optional. A filesystem metadata read can remain pending after Node delivers both
the refusal and the child close.

The third general audit identified this liveness defect. It did not observe a
naturally stalled Windows filesystem. The earlier output-loss and help-only failure
corrections remain necessary and retain their existing precedence.

## Decision

Give optional diagnosis a private absolute monotonic deadline 1,000 ms after the
runner observes a genuine no-PID refusal. It applies independently of the caller's
request timeout, including null. Timely factual observations retain the existing
fixed cause. On expiry return the actual spawn code with unknown cause and definite
non-submission. Expiry does not mean that a process timed out, was cancelled or had
a missing executable/directory.

Check the elapsed budget before each metadata lookup, when accepting its result and
when the diagnostic timer runs. A delayed event-loop callback cannot make late
metadata timely. Earlier request deadlines and cancellation settle promptly through
the existing outcome rules. Every settlement clears the owned diagnostic timer and
removes the abort listener. Late metadata cannot change the result or initiate a
follow-on lookup. Node may still finish an already issued native `stat`; this bounds
the wait, without claiming filesystem cancellation.

Started-process output loss, uncertain delivery and stronger failures retain their
existing behavior. There is no additional launch, kill of a nonexistent child,
retry, fallback, PATH resolver, dependency or public configuration option.

## Alternatives

- Rely on the request timeout or watchdog: declined because supported defaults
  provide neither bound.
- Return unknown immediately for every refusal: declined because fast local
  metadata provides useful factual diagnoses without further execution.
- Use synchronous filesystem access or a new worker/process subsystem: declined
  because either blocking the event loop or adding an execution boundary is
  disproportionate to this optional diagnostic.
- Add user-facing configuration or automatic retry: declined because a known failed
  start needs a conservative terminal result, not another turn or policy choice.

## Consequences

One second allows ordinary local metadata while bounding the known refusal under
default settings. Slow or unavailable metadata produces the existing generic
unknown-cause failure instead of a specific diagnosis. The event loop must run to
deliver any JavaScript result; the monotonic check prevents late cause acceptance
when it resumes. This is neither a hard real-time guarantee nor native stat cancellation.

Maintained tests exercise the public harness and real runner with successful
prerequisites, a refused default turn and a controlled pending stat, plus timely and
late metadata, earlier deadlines/abort, cleanup and started-process controls. An
old-source control must fail the finite default-turn liveness oracle. Controlled
metadata delays remain distinct from native refusal observations and a naturally
occurring filesystem stall. No schema, stored-content, environment, coverage-policy
or owner acceptance change is required. Independent corrective review, separate QA,
current CI/native verification and coordinator completion remain delivery gates.
